name: Rice and what goes with it

lineages.name: Rice cooked with things in it

origin.era: said to begin as a way to stretch rice (Nara's account)

cells.what: Rice cooked together with vegetables, fish or chestnuts, or rice with a topping poured over
cells.rice: Inside it; the rice is the dish
cells.regional: Ehime's tai-meshi is cooked-in in Tōyo and poured-over raw in Nanyo; Nara calls soy-seasoned versions iro-gohan
cells.know: The origin of kamameshi as a dish is not settled in any source I could use

origin.era: zōni with mochi at New Year from the Heian period (ministry account)

cells.what: Pounded glutinous rice, the New Year soup it goes into, and glutinous rice coloured with beans
cells.rice: Made from rice; eaten at festivals and celebrations
cells.regional: Square mochi east, round mochi west, roughly at Sekigahara, with exceptions; Hokkaido sekihan is sweet
cells.know: The Consumer Affairs Agency has issued a New Year warning about choking on mochi

origin.era: two traditional stories for nattō, unsettled

cells.what: Soy milk set with a coagulant; boiled soybeans fermented with nattō bacteria
cells.rice: Nattō is eaten with soy sauce or in soup; Mito’s small beans are said to cling to rice
cells.regional: Mito sells small beans and straw-wrapped nattō; Yamagata makes nattō soup; Kyoto’s tera-nattō is a salty, dried kind
cells.know: Momen tofu is broken up and pressed; kinugoshi is set as it is

lineages.name: Pickles, tsukudani and furikake
lineages.nameJa: 漬物・佃煮・ふりかけ

origin.place: Nationwide; Kyoto pickles; Tsukudajima and Osaka’s Tsukuda village for tsukudani
origin.era: tsukudani linked to fishermen from Tsukuda village in the Edo period (told several ways)

cells.what: Salted, fermented or seasoned vegetables; small fish and seaweed simmered down in soy; dry seasonings to sprinkle
cells.rice: Pickles are part of the basic one-soup, three-dish meal; tsukudani goes in ochazuke and onigiri
cells.regional: Smoked iburi-gakko in Akita, salt-free sunki in Kiso, Kyoto’s senmaizuke, suguki and shibazuke
cells.know: The origin of furikake could not be confirmed from an industry or company source

cells.what: Pork miso soup, kenchin-jiru, noppe, clam soup, dango-jiru
cells.rice: The ‘one soup’ of the one-soup, three-dish meal
cells.regional: Kenchin-jiru differs between Kanagawa and Iwate; Shimane and Shiga use different clams
